_doc: #642 THE ONE DECLARATION of the Store's read-only feeds: the repo's COMMITS and its CI-CD runs. Read by FeedViewer; nothing in Kotlin names a repository, an endpoint, a JSON field or a status word. One tab per entry, in this order, so a third feed (releases, issues, a second repo) is an entry here and no Kotlin at all. FeedViewer is a READER: every row's action is 'open the link the feed itself gave us', so there is nothing here that can install, write or authenticate. That is why these endpoints are the unauthenticated public ones - a token would buy nothing a reader needs and would be one more secret on the device.
_doc_transport: #668 THESE URLS ARE THE ANONYMOUS GITHUB API, AND THAT IS THE KNOWN DEFECT. Anonymous api.github.com is capped at 60 requests/hour PER IP, and an exhausted quota answers 403 with 'API rate limit exceeded for <ip>' - which is the 403 reported on both feeds. Measured 2026-09-30: the same endpoint returned 200 with x-ratelimit-limit 60 / remaining 55, so this is quota exhaustion that self-heals when the window rolls, NOT a permissions problem and NOT a bug in the reader. Note the quota is per IP and the phone shares it with everything else on that address, so unrelated tooling on the same network can spend the Store's budget. THE FIX IS THE TRANSPORT: route these through the fleet's git-proxy-api (#647), which holds the fleet's own GitHub credential server-side so the phone holds none, and authenticate machine-to-machine with Authorization: Bearer (NOT the browser session path, which #655 breaks by dropping the /git prefix on the Authelia return). THAT PROXY CANNOT SERVE THESE TWO FEEDS YET: it exposes exactly /git/health, /git/endpoints, /git/repos and /git/repos/:owner/:repo/tarball, and its router refuses to start unless served routes equal declared ones, so commits and actions/runs must first be added to runtime.endpoints plus handlers in the cloud-u-containers repo. Until they exist, repointing these urls would turn a self-healing 403 into a permanent 404. When they do exist (#674), adopting them is ONLY setting the two `proxy` values here - no Kotlin. `url` is NEVER repointed at the fleet: the proxy is tried first and any proxy failure falls through to the public `url`, because reading public data must not require the fleet to be up (#662 makes the proxy sheddable). ONE OPEN QUESTION FOR #674: every non-health git-proxy-api route today is authelia_bearer and this reader sends no credential, so if the new routes keep that gate, adoption also needs a credential path into the reader - until then the proxy would answer 401 and every read would land on the public fallback, still correct but not yet quota-free. EVERY FAILURE SAYS WHICH ONE IT IS (FeedViewer.explain): quota (429, or 403 with Retry-After or X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0), unreachable (no connection), not found, refused, or a body without the declared array. None of them draws as an empty feed; 'nothing in this feed' is reserved for a 2xx that carried an empty list. DO NOT add a cache to soften the 403: a stale feed presented as live is worse than a feed that says it could not read.
_doc_fields: `url` is fetched through SourceResolver.getBody, the store's one request path. `per_page` is part of the declared url, so the page size is a data edit like everything else (raised 30 -> 50 for #668). `items` names the array inside the response; omit it when the response IS the array (GitHub's /commits). `title`/`subtitle`/`ref`/`link` are templates: every {a.b.c} is looked up as a dotted path in the item and substituted, and a path the item does not carry substitutes empty - so a feed that changes shape degrades to a thinner row instead of crashing the tab. `ref` is the short identifier drawn at the head of the row (a sha, a run number). `state` is the field whose value is matched against `ok`/`bad` below to colour the row; a value in neither list is drawn neutral, which is what an in-flight run must look like - 'not finished' is not 'failed'.

feeds.label: Commits
feeds.blurb: The repository's commit feed, newest first. Read-only: a row opens the commit on GitHub.
feeds.title: {commit.message}
feeds.subtitle: {commit.author.name}  ·  {commit.author.date}

feeds.label: CI · CD
feeds.blurb: The CI-CD run feed, newest first. A run still going is drawn neutral, not red — unfinished is not failed. A row opens the run's own log page.
feeds.title: {name}
feeds.subtitle: {status}  ·  {conclusion}  ·  {created_at}

_doc_proxy: #841 ADOPTED (#674 shipped GET /git/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits and /runs on api.diegonmarcos.com, per_page 1-50). `proxy` is now an object: its `url` is tried FIRST with the fleet Authelia bearer (the host hands FeedViewer.fleetBearer the same token its other fleet calls send), and its other fields describe the proxy's REDUCED body - {commits:[{sha,message,author,date,html_url}]} and {runs:[{name,display_title,status,conclusion,created_at,html_url,path}]} - inheriting any field it leaves out. Errors there are {error,code}: 401 missing_authorization, 403 repo_not_declared, 502 upstream_error. ANY proxy failure (no bearer, 401, 403, 404, 502, unreachable, wrong shape) falls through to the public `url`, and the tab shows THAT read's own error, with the proxy's appended. per_page stays in the urls, so page size is still a data edit on both legs.
